---
title: "Trait retrieval"
---

```{python}
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
from _lib import *
P = read("params.csv")
iid = P[P["errmodel"] == "iid"].copy()
iid["label"] = iid["sample_id"].map(sample_label)
MEAS = ["Cab", "Car", "Cw", "Cm"]
```

Every backend fitted the same PROSPECT-D model (iid normal residuals) to
reflectance only. Here the posteriors of the four constituents with measured
values are compared with those measurements. Points are posterior medians;
bars are central 90% credible intervals.

```{python}
#| label: fig-traits
#| fig-cap: "Posterior median and 90% credible interval vs. measured value, by backend (color and marker). The gray line is 1:1. Both axes are logarithmic. The white/variegated Cornus leaf, measured at Car = 0, cannot be shown on the log axis but is included in the tables. Click legend entries to hide backends."
fig = make_subplots(rows=2, cols=2, horizontal_spacing=0.1, vertical_spacing=0.14,
                    subplot_titles=[f"{TRAIT_NAME[p]} ({TRAIT_UNITS[p]})" for p in MEAS])
offsets = dict(zip(BACKENDS, np.linspace(-0.03, 0.03, len(BACKENDS))))
for i, p in enumerate(MEAS):
    r, c = i // 2 + 1, i % 2 + 1
    d0 = iid[(iid["param"] == p) & (iid["measured"] > 0)]
    lo, hi = d0[["measured", "q05"]].min().min(), d0[["measured", "q95"]].max().max()
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=[lo / 1.5, hi * 1.5], y=[lo / 1.5, hi * 1.5], mode="lines",
                             line=dict(color=AXIS, width=1), hoverinfo="skip", showlegend=False), r, c)
    for b in BACKENDS:
        d = d0[d0["backend"] == b]
        if d.empty:
            continue
        x = d["measured"] * 10 ** offsets[b]
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=x, y=d["q50"], mode="markers", name=LABEL[b], legendgroup=b, showlegend=(i == 0),
            marker=dict(color=COLOR[b], symbol=SYMBOL[b], size=8, line=dict(color=SURFACE, width=1)),
            error_y=dict(type="data", symmetric=False, array=d["q95"] - d["q50"],
                         arrayminus=d["q50"] - d["q05"], color=COLOR[b], thickness=1.5, width=0),
            customdata=np.c_[d["label"], d["measured"], d["q05"], d["q95"]],
            hovertemplate=("%{customdata[0]}<br>measured %{customdata[1]:.3g}<br>median %{y:.3g}"
                           "<br>90% CI %{customdata[2]:.3g} – %{customdata[3]:.3g}<extra>" + LABEL[b] + "</extra>")),
            r, c)
    tv = log_ticks(lo / 1.5, hi * 1.5)
    fig.update_xaxes(type="log", title_text="measured", tickvals=tv, ticktext=[f"{v:g}" for v in tv], row=r, col=c)
    fig.update_yaxes(type="log", title_text="posterior", tickvals=tv, ticktext=[f"{v:g}" for v in tv], row=r, col=c)
fig.update_layout(height=760, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.08, x=0))
show(fig)
```

## Accuracy and calibration

```{python}
#| label: tbl-trait-skill
#| tbl-cap: "Retrieval skill by backend and trait over all samples with a measured value, synthetic leaf included. Relative bias is the median of (posterior median − measured) / measured, over samples with measured > 0. Coverage counts how many measured values fall inside the 90% credible interval."
rows = []
for b in BACKENDS:
    for p in MEAS:
        d = iid[(iid["backend"] == b) & (iid["param"] == p) & iid["measured"].notna()]
        if d.empty:
            continue
        pos = d[d["measured"] > 0]
        rows.append({"Backend": LABEL[b], "Trait": p, "n": len(d),
                     "RMSE": np.sqrt(np.mean((d["q50"] - d["measured"])**2)),
                     "Median rel. bias": np.median((pos["q50"] - pos["measured"]) / pos["measured"]),
                     "Spearman ρ": d[["q50", "measured"]].corr("spearman").iloc[0, 1],
                     "90% coverage": f"{int(d['covered90'].sum())}/{len(d)}",
                     "Median 90% CI width (rel.)": np.median((d["q95"] - d["q05"]) / d["q50"])})
skill = pd.DataFrame(rows)
show_table(fmt_table(skill, 3))
```

```{python}
cov = iid[iid["param"].isin(MEAS) & iid["measured"].notna() & (iid["sample_id"] != "synthetic")]
cov_rate = cov["covered90"].mean()
syn = iid[(iid["sample_id"] == "synthetic") & iid["measured"].notna()]
syn_cov = syn["covered90"].mean()
```

::: {.callout-important}
## The iid error model gives over-confident trait posteriors

On the synthetic spectrum, where the iid model is the true data-generating
process, the 90% intervals cover the truth
`{python} f"{100*syn_cov:.0f}%"` of the time, across all backends and
parameters. On the real leaves only `{python} f"{100*cov_rate:.0f}%"` of
measured Cab/Car/EWT/LMA values fall inside the 90% intervals. Part of that is
measurement error in the reference traits and PROSPECT's structural error. But
the intervals are also far too narrow: they are typically a few percent wide,
because the iid likelihood treats 2000+ strongly autocorrelated residuals as
independent pieces of information. See [Error models](error-models.qmd).
:::
